To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the O2 abundance is low in the rho Oph A molecular cloud, but the derived O2 column densities are consistent with predictions of PDR models.
the O2 emission toward rho Oph originates in the densest and warmest regions of this star forming cloud.
the Herschel HIFI observations confirm the Odin detections of O2 toward the rho Oph A star-forming core, and that O2 is detected toward only half the area covered by the HIFI beam.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first detection of O2 in the interstellar medium at submillimeter and far infrared wavelengths.
the detection of O2 and the determination of its abundance toward rho OphA, the most prominent molecular cloud in the rho Ophiuchi complex.

the following questions: (a) What is the origin of the O2 emission? (b) Is it possible to explain the O2 emission with standard chemical cloud models? (c) What is the physical and chemical structure of the O2-emitting region?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the O2 emission is not coming from a well-defined, compact source but is spread out over an area comparable to the extent of the rho Oph A cloud core.
O2 is present in rho Oph, but that its origin and distribution is not fully resolved yet.
the Herschel observations of O2 in the rho Oph A region do not support the presence of pure gas-phase chemical models.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the observed line emission is consistent with the presence of O2 in the cold gas phase, and the derived O2 abundances agree with the expectations from chemical cloud models, but the observed line intensities are too high to be consistent with the models.
the observed line intensities of the three detected O2 lines are in agreement with the predictions of the chemical models.
the Herschel data do not support the presence of significant amounts of O2 in the rho Oph A cloud.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast with the predictions of standard models of pure gas-phase cloud chemistry, O2 is not ubiquitous in the dense interstellar medium and is only present in a small fraction of the molecular gas.
, in contrast to earlier expectations, O2 is not a good tracer of the dense gas in rho Oph.
the O2 emission is spatially well confined, and that its abundance in rho Oph is relatively high.
